title: Volkswagen's replacement for the ID.4 crossover is here
gist: VW is replacing the ID.4 with the ID. Tiguan on the MEB+ platform (58/77 kWh, up to 373 miles WLTP), priced from 42,695 euros in Germany with European launch early 2027 and no US timing. It returns physical controls and normal door handles, possibly driven by Chinese regulators.

insights.claim: Volkswagen has sold almost a million ID.4 and ID.5 vehicles globally and is replacing them with the ID. Tiguan, borrowing its best-selling model's name.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Rebranding EVs under ICE nameplates aims to mainstream EV demand.

insights.claim: The ID. Tiguan uses the updated MEB+ platform with 58 or 77 kWh packs, up to 295 hp AWD and up to 373 miles WLTP range.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Competitive specs for the mass-market EV crossover segment.

insights.claim: German pricing starts at 42,695 euros, with European pre-sales next week and launch in early 2027; North American timing and pricing are unannounced.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: No near-term US contribution; Chattanooga has shifted away from ID.4.

insights.claim: VW wants the ID. Tiguan to feel premium rather than mainstream, under a new 'Pure Positive' design language.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Premiumization attempt to protect EV margins.

insights.claim: VW is returning to physical buttons, climate switches, window switches and air vents, reflecting customer feedback against touch controls.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.locator: The return to normal door handles

insights.claim: The return to normal door handles may have been driven by Chinese vehicle regulators.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Chinese regulations are shaping global vehicle design.
insights.quote: The return to normal door handles will be welcome, even if it might have been driven by Chinese vehicle regulators.
insights.locator: The return to normal door handles

insights.claim: VW's Chattanooga, Tennessee plant turned its attention away from the ID.4 earlier this year.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: US EV production by VW is scaling back.
